key_insight: RMT augments Vision Transformer attention with explicit spatial priors using a Manhattan-distance decay, enabling attention to respect image geometry while reducing redundant global interactions.
problem_solved: Addresses ViT's lack of explicit spatial bias and the high quadratic cost of vanilla self-attention, making transformers more spatially aware and computationally efficient for vision tasks.
method: Inject Manhattan-distance decay into attention weights to bias interactions toward nearby tokens and encode spatial locality.
Introduce a structured token-mixing component (horizontal-oriented factorization) to capture directional spatial patterns and limit full pairwise attention.
Combine the spatially-decayed attention with standard ViT blocks to form RMT, a general-purpose backbone that preserves representational power with lower overhead.
impact: Makes ViT-style backbones more practical for real-world vision workloads by improving spatial reasoning and lowering computational cost—beneficial for model designers, deployers, and downstream task performance.

paper_title: Advancing Vision Transformer with Enhanced Spatial Priors
paper_authors: Qihang Fan, Huaibo Huang, Mingrui Chen, Hongmin Liu, Ran He
